_comments: Declares Journal Entries -> Journal Entry Lines as a related-record collection (MJ 6.1).
CodeGen reads RelatedRecordCollection and emits a typed `Lines` accessor onto the GENERATED
entity class, so both tiers get it. That replaces the hand-rolled collection on
LoadLines — which existed only on the server, so the Angular JE editor had to reach through a
service layer to compose an entry it could not model directly.
This is the case MJ's own documentation uses as the worked example for a cross-record
invariant: debits must equal credits, validated over the complete set before the first row is
written. Declared here, that check runs in the BROWSER too.
RelatedEntity and RelatedEntityJoinField are deliberately NOT set here — they are already
columns on this same row (Journal Entry Lines / JournalEntryID). Duplicating them would create
two sources of truth with the JSON copy winning silently.
Sequence maintains LineNumber, which UQ_JournalEntryLine_JE_LineNumber requires to be unique
per entry and the column requires to be NOT NULL.
Keyed by entity NAMES rather than the row's ID: EntityRelationship IDs are minted by CodeGen,
so a hardcoded UUID would stop matching the first time the database is rebuilt from zero.
